“Chaos isnʼt the enemy. Stagnation is.” The Stormlash Veldt isn't about madness or mysticism—itʼs raw, unrefined energy. It rewards speed, ingenuity, and timing. There is a rhythm to survival here—those who fight it are crushed. Those who adapt become charged. Itʼs an ideal zone to test powers gained in earlier zones, to introduce unique weather-linked gear, and to foreshadow upcoming multiversal transitions.

Safe resting areas are rare in Ashland. Finding caves, sheltered ruins, or bunkers adds a layer of strategy, with players needing to plan when and where to rest. This Ashland guide provides players and GMs with all the tools needed to explore a desolate, volatile environment full of hazards, hidden dangers, and resources. With its mix of ash-covered terrain, hostile wildlife, and unpredictable ground shifts, the Ashland setting challenges players to survive and adapt in a landscape shaped by fire and destruction. volcanic glass scattered across the ground, but scavenging attracts predators.

records.proposedName: 1.Use the Unpredictable Terrain to Build Tension
records.summary: Describe the constant movement of asteroids and unpredictable paths to keep players on edge. Encourage careful planning as they navigate the chaotic environment. 2.Emphasize Resource Management: Scavenging for oxygen, radiation protection, and fuel is critical in an asteroid field. Reinforce the high-risk, high-reward nature of resource collection and make players weigh the costs of staying too long.

•The Arborae did not fight in direct combat but instead used nature as their weapon. •They grew forests back overnight, cutting off goblin supply lines and isolating their forces. •They commanded massive plant creatures, poisoned industrial sites, and altered the land itself to reject goblin structures. •Havalaeaʼs climate turned against the goblins, with monsoons, shifting terrain, and aggressive wildlife acting as additional obstacles. •Arborae warriors, physically connected to the environment, could phase into trees, manipulate roots, and move unseen through their own domain.

1.Camp Layout: •Tents and Shelters: Simple cloth or leather structures provide shelter but are vulnerable to weather and attack. •Fire Pits and Cooking Areas: Centralized for warmth and cooking, these can draw attention or pose a fire hazard if not properly managed. •Supply Wagons: Carry essential goods like food, tools, and medicine, but may be in limited supply and protected by guards. •Livestock Pens: If the camp has animals, they are often kept in makeshift pens, which may attract predators.
